exposure: three-dimensional placental volume (S1 and S2 sectors)
cohort: The study included 150 singleton pregnancies delivered in the third trimester, all diagnosed with complete placenta previa.
finding: Decreased cervical canal length, increased cervical canal dilation, and altered three-dimensional placental volume (decreased S1, increased S2) were significant independent risk factors for placenta accreta spectrum and severe peripartum hemorrhage in patients with complete placenta previa.
